title: How do you virtually stage a room with AI so it doesn't look fake?
description: Virtual staging gets spotted because of lighting, not furniture. Tell the model where the light already is, then nail the furniture to the floor with contact shadows.

faq.q: Why does virtual staging look fake?
faq.a: Almost always lighting, not furniture. The sofa is lit from a window the room doesn't have, so shadows fall the wrong way. Your eye catches the contradiction before your brain names it, and the whole photo reads as a lie.

faq.q: What single line most improves an AI staging prompt?
faq.a: A contact-shadow instruction — 'dark contact shadows where legs, rug edge and console meet the floor.' Furniture rendered without contact shadows floats above the floor, which is the difference between a room and a collage.
